canonical_question: How does the 'single phase random solid solution' of the SPS sample compare in hardness and yield strength to the multi-phase oxygen-rich samples?

question_variants.question: How does the 'single phase random solid solution' of the SPS sample compare in hardness and yield strength to the multi-phase oxygen-rich samples?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The single-phase random solid solution sample (MA-SPS-HPT) has a hardness of 584 HV10. However, specific yield strength data is not reported for this sample or the multi-phase oxygen-rich samples in the provided evidence, making a full comparison of yield strength impossible.

answers.answer: The MA-SPS-HPT specimen (single phase bcc solid solution with oxides) has a hardness of 584 HV10. The text attributes this high hardness to high oxygen content and oxide particles. No yield strength values are reported in the evidence spans to compare against the multi-phase oxygen-rich samples.
answers.conditions: High oxygen content, High Pressure Torsion
answers.mechanism: High oxygen content in solid solution and presence of oxide particles caused additional strengthening
answers.boundary_limitation: Specimen broken during HPT process, results disputable
evidence_spans: Very high hardness of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen (584 HV10) can be ascribed to the high oxygen content in solid solution and also the presence of oxide particles that caused additional strengthening.
As seen in Figure 8 hardness was correlated with oxygen content in the sample.
It should be pointed out that the MA-SPS-HPT specimen was broken into several pieces during the HPT process and therefore the results of such specimen are disputable.
